C-BROWSER-DOWNLOADS-COOKIES-SERVICES-202.IntentSummary: Deliver the second bounded M1.3 browser-service slice: implement independent downloads and cookies/site-data service plugins above the existing M1.2 browser engine primitives, decomposed into dependency-ordered packages P1 through P4.

T-001.Title: Extend ADR-BROWSER-SERVICE-PLUGINS-V1 with downloads, cookies, site-data, artifact handoff, and secret redaction architecture

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: ADR documents downloads and cookies/site-data service boundaries, DownloadRecordId vs engine DownloadId, opaque ArtifactRef handoff without path authority, cookie metadata vs secret value authority separation, redacted Debug representation for cookie secrets, and incomplete outcome post-crash reconciliation.

T-002.Title: Extend worldline-browser-services-contract with experimental v0.1 downloads, cookies, and site-data contracts

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: worldline-browser-services-contract defines browser.downloads/0.1 with DownloadRecordId, lifecycle states, progress/reconciliation DTOs, and opaque ArtifactRef without host path leaks.
worldline-browser-services-contract defines browser.cookies/0.1 separating CookieMetadata from CookieValue, with redacted Debug representation on secret value containers.
worldline-browser-services-contract defines browser.site-data/0.1 with context/origin-scoped ClearSiteData operations.
Authority identifiers distinguish downloads read vs control, cookies metadata read vs secret value read vs mutation vs admin policy, and site-data clear.

T-003.Title: Add contract wire, secret redaction, and authority separation acceptance tests in worldline-browser-services-contract

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Compatibility tests prove JSON wire stability for experimental 0.1 downloads, cookies, and site-data requests/responses.
Diagnostic tests prove that CookieValue Debug formatting redacts secret values to prevent plaintext leakage in logs/traces.
Authority separation tests verify cookie metadata authority does not grant secret value read, cookie mutation, or site data clearing.

T-004.Title: Implement worldline-browser-downloads plugin state machine, DownloadRecordId persistence, and capability RPC

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: worldline-browser-downloads manages DownloadRecordId lifecycle (Pending, Active, Paused, Completed, Cancelled, Failed, Reconciling).
Durable download intent/record is committed to transactional installation state before invoking non-idempotent engine operations.
Durable records persist only bounded product metadata (PageId, URL, suggested filename, media type, byte counts, lifecycle, engine DownloadId, ArtifactRef) and do not store host destination paths.

T-005.Title: Implement engine download hook integration, opaque artifact materialization, and crash reconciliation in worldline-browser-downloads

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Completed downloads are materialized through the generic host blob/artifact mechanism returning an opaque ArtifactRef to consumers rather than a filesystem path.
Staging cleanup operates safely within the authorized staging root.
Service restart reconciles non-terminal downloads against engine state and marks uncertain outcomes as Reconciling without automatically restarting downloads.
Redelivered engine download facts do not produce duplicate DownloadRecordId entries.

T-006.Title: Add downloads service acceptance suite covering durable intent, lifecycle, opaque artifact handoff, and recovery

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Acceptance tests verify start, pause, resume, cancel, lifecycle progression, durable intent before engine start, crash recovery reconciliation, and failure isolation.
Tests prove that possession of DownloadRecordId or download-read authority does not grant artifact content byte read authority without independent blob-read authority.

T-007.Title: Implement worldline-browser-cookies plugin metadata inspection, secret value disclosure, and capability RPC

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: worldline-browser-cookies exposes distinct capability RPC operations for metadata inspection (GetCookieMetadata), secret value disclosure (GetCookieValue), mutation (SetCookie/DeleteCookie), and policy administration.
Cookie metadata responses contain no raw cookie value.
Debug and diagnostic representations of types carrying cookie values are strictly redacted.

T-008.Title: Implement context-scoped cookie engine projection, origin site-data clear, and cross-context isolation in worldline-browser-cookies

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Cookie and site-data operations validate exact BrowserContextId and canonical URL/origin/domain scope.
Chromium profile cookie store (engine.cookies/0.1) remains the source of truth for cookie values; the service does not persist a second cookie database.
browser.site-data/0.1 clears context/origin-scoped storage via engine.storage/0.1 without affecting unrelated contexts, download records, tabs, or history.
Cross-context access is strictly denied even when visiting the same origin/host.

T-009.Title: Add cookies and site-data service acceptance suite covering authority separation, redaction, cross-context isolation, and restart

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Acceptance tests verify metadata-only readers cannot access cookie values, cross-context access is denied, secret redaction is preserved, site-data clearing is isolated, and restarting cookies service reloads from engine store without data corruption.

T-010.Title: Implement bounded proving slice S3B in worldline-reference

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Proving slice S3B executes end-to-end against the real M1.2 browser provider on loopback content: start download -> durable DownloadRecordId -> complete artifact -> verify bytes -> restart downloads service -> verify record persists.
S3B proves download metadata authority cannot read completed artifact bytes without blob read authority.

S3B creates two isolated contexts for same origin with distinct cookies, proves metadata vs value authority separation, restarts cookies service, and verifies values remain engine-authoritative and context-isolated.
S3B writes localStorage in both contexts, clears one context via browser.site-data/0.1, and proves other context remains untouched.
S3B proves terminating downloads or cookies service leaves direct navigation, tabs, and history operational.

T-011.Title: Integrate downloads, cookies, site-data and S3B into BrowserServices CI suite, architecture guard, and workflows

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Invoke-WorldlineCi BrowserServices suite includes worldline-browser-downloads, worldline-browser-cookies, and S3B acceptance tests.
Test-WorldlineArchitecture.ps1 verifies kernel and CEF do not depend on worldline-browser-downloads, worldline-browser-cookies, DownloadRecordId, or cookie policy.
PR and master workflows run BrowserServices suite cross-platform without public network access.

T-012.Title: Run full target verification and reconcile documentation

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: README is updated with M1.3 downloads and cookies/site-data browser services documentation.
Full repository verification passes for all suites (BrowserServices, Source, Correctness, ArchitectureSecurity, ProvingSlice, RealChromium, BrowserProvider, All).
